ground_truth: A 22-year-old male came in with persistent blackheads (comedonal acne). There are no inflamed papules, pustules, or nodules, the acne looks stable, and there is no scarring left behind by earlier inflammation. Following the 2024 dermatology guidelines, the plan is a topical retinoid together with benzoyl peroxide. He was counselled on the stepwise treatment approach and on keeping up maintenance therapy so the acne doesn't come back. Because the blackheads are mild, oral isotretinoin should be stopped. He is to apply adapalene 0.1% gel every night over the whole affected area, and use a benzoyl peroxide 2.5% wash once each morning. Improvement should show within 8-12 weeks of steady use, after which maintenance continues 2-3 times a week. A follow-up visit is set for 2 months, and if the skin gets irritated he can drop to every other night for a while.
